reel: The Pig War of 1859: the US and Britain almost went to war over one pig on San Juan Island; the pig was the only casualty
status: 13 files downloaded and viewed (9 via the Wikimedia Commons API with licence confirmed from extmetadata, 4 originals pulled straight from nps.gov/sajh). Two colour modern photos of the camps, one colour 1868 watercolour, four period B&W photos/sketches (1859, 1866, c.1868, 1872), two maps (1859 Admiralty chart + NPS claims map), two portraits, one primary document (Cutlar's 1859 affidavit, NARA). No real film of the 1859 events exists (predates cinema); the only video found is modern explainer packages, which were not kept.

assets.what_it_shows: COLOUR. The white two-storey Royal Marine blockhouse of English Camp standing at the water's edge of Garrison Bay, bright green lawn and driftwood fence rails in front, dark fir forest and blue water behind, two visitors on the path at left.
assets.best_segments: THE OPENER. Push in on the blockhouse (centre, x 1900-3800) for the first 2 s; a 9:16 crop at x 2000-4250 keeps blockhouse + water. Landscape, so plan a slow zoom rather than a static crop.

assets.license: Public domain, US National Park Service work (Commons {{PD-USGov-NPS}}; NPGallery upload, EXIF 2013-12-04)
assets.license_note: US federal government work, no restrictions.
assets.what_it_shows: COLOUR. The golden American Camp prairie on San Juan Island's south end, a strip of blue water, forested shore and snow-capped Mount Baker on the horizon. Shot in winter light; slight haze.
assets.best_segments: Second-location shot ('the Americans dug in on this prairie'). 9:16 crop centred on Mt Baker (x 900-2270) keeps grass + peak. Could also open the reel if a wide landscape beat is wanted.

assets.license: Public domain: 1868 watercolour by Edwin Augustus Porcher RN (d. 1878), PD-old; scan published by the National Park Service on nps.gov/sajh
assets.license_note: NPS page caption: 'An 1868 painting of English Camp by E.L. Porcher, who then a junior officer aboard HMS Sparrowhawk.' Artist dead >70 years; NPS scan carries no restriction.
assets.credit_line: E. A. Porcher, 1868, courtesy National Park Service
assets.what_it_shows: COLOUR period artwork. Garrison Bay from the hillside: the camp's white buildings and the blockhouse on the shore, a tall flagpole, the formal garden terrace up the hill, a square-rigged ship at anchor and a rowing boat with Royal Navy sailors in the foreground, warm yellow sky.
assets.best_segments: Best 'what English Camp looked like at the time' beat. Pan from the rowing boat (bottom centre) up to the blockhouse and flagpole (x 2000-2700). 9:16 crop x 1800-3870 keeps boat, blockhouse and hill.

assets.license: Public domain: photograph taken September 1859, PD-old; published by the National Park Service
assets.license_note: NPS caption: 'Belle Vue Sheep Farm during the height of the Pig War crisis in September 1859. At far right is the British magistrate, John De Courcy. next to him is the U.S. Civil Magistrate from Whatcom County, Henry Crosbie.' Two-frame panorama, low contrast, only 674 px tall.
assets.credit_line: Photo, September 1859, courtesy National Park Service
assets.what_it_shows: B&W, two joined frames marked 'No 2' and 'No 1'. Men in hats sit and lean on a split-rail fence in front of the whitewashed Hudson's Bay Company farm buildings; a tent and a picket fence at right. The actual place and month of the standoff.
assets.best_segments: The 'this is the farm, during the crisis' beat. Use the right-hand frame (x 1030-2000) as a 9:16 crop with heavy push-in; it is small, so keep it to 1-2 s.

assets.license: Public domain: photograph c.1868, PD-old; published by the National Park Service
assets.license_note: NPS caption: 'The American Camp parade ground area, circa 1868. The lone remaining building is the Officers' Quarters at far left.'
assets.credit_line: Photo, c.1868, courtesy National Park Service
assets.what_it_shows: B&W. Wide view of the American Camp parade ground: tall flagpole at left, a row of white barracks and officers' buildings behind a long white picket fence, a lone soldier lying in the grass, stumps and scrub in the foreground.
assets.best_segments: The 'American Camp' beat during the joint occupation. Slow pan left-to-right along the buildings; 9:16 crop around the flagpole (x 50-670).

assets.license: Public domain (Commons extmetadata: pd; 1866 drawing photographed by Asahel Curtis, via Northwest Digital Heritage / DPLA)
assets.license_note: Original caption on the image: 'The R.M.L.I. Camp at San Juan Island, December 1866'. PD-old on both the drawing and the Curtis photo.
assets.credit_line: Sketch, 1866, Asahel Curtis photo, via DPLA / Wikimedia Commons
assets.what_it_shows: B&W pen sketch, very wide. English Camp from the water: huge Union Jack on the flagpole, the blockhouse on the shore, marines drilling, barracks, forest covering the hill, canoes on Garrison Bay.
assets.best_segments: The 'the British built a camp at the other end of the island' beat. Crop tightly on the flag + blockhouse (x 1900-2900) for 9:16; wide pan otherwise.

assets.license: Public domain (Commons extmetadata: pd; 1872 photograph reproduced in an 1899 book, scanned by Internet Archive)
assets.license_note: PD-old. Halftone from a book, so grainy; fine at 1-2 s with motion.
assets.credit_line: Photo, 1872, via Internet Archive / Wikimedia Commons
assets.what_it_shows: B&W. About 30 Royal Marines in a single line with white cross-belts and rifles at order arms, an officer at each end, white barracks and a wooded hill behind: the garrison at English Camp before the 1872 withdrawal.
assets.best_segments: Use for 'the only British soldiers who ever fought here... never fired a shot' or the withdrawal beat. 9:16 crop on the centre of the line (x 350-1010), slow push.

assets.license: Public domain (Commons extmetadata: pd; UK Hydrographic Office chart published 1859, Crown copyright expired)
assets.license_note: PD-old. 69 MB file; downscale before use. Scan originates from a map dealer (raremaps.com) but a faithful reproduction of a PD 2-D work carries no new copyright.
assets.what_it_shows: The period map of the dispute: 'Haro and Rosario Straits, surveyed by Captn. G.H. Richards and the officers of HMS Plumper 1858-9'. Vancouver Island at left, San Juan Island in the centre, both straits labelled, Juan de Fuca Strait at the bottom.
assets.best_segments: Map beat: zoom from the whole chart into San Juan Island (around x 7000-8500, y 13500-15500), then slide between the 'HARO' label (west of San Juan) and 'ROSARIO STRAIT' (east). Overlay the two claim lines as graphics.

assets.license: Public domain, US National Park Service graphic (nps.gov/sajh)
assets.what_it_shows: COLOUR modern diagram: British Columbia / Washington Territory, the undisputed 49th-parallel boundary in black, the American claim through Haro Strait in blue, the British claim through Rosario Strait in red, San Juan Island arrowed between them; legend bottom-left.
assets.best_segments: Clean explainer map for the 'two channels, one word' beat. Square, so crop to the islands (x 600-1400, y 300-1100 of 1400-px preview) for 9:16; or use as a full-frame insert.

assets.best_segments: Portrait beat for 'Captain George Pickett landed with 64 men'. Crop the face (x 1500-3900, y 1000-4400).

assets.license_note: LOW RESOLUTION (379x552). Usable only as a small inset or a 1 s beat with grain; no larger copy obtained.

assets.best_segments: Inset for the Baynes line ('would not involve two great nations in a war over a squabble about a pig'). Keep small or heavily stylised.

assets.license: Public domain, US National Archives (Records of the Adjutant General's Office; NARA Flickr Commons upload; Commons extmetadata: pd)
assets.what_it_shows: Handwritten copy of Lyman Cutlar's sworn affidavit, 7 Sept 1859: 'That on or about the 15th of last June he shot a hog belonging to the Hudson Bay Company ... Mr Griffin very much enraged said the only way it could be settled would be by him paying one hundred dollars.' (Page 3, not downloaded, adds: 'pay one hundred dollars for an animal that was not worth ten'.)
assets.best_segments: Document beat: tilt down the page and land on the last lines ('one hundred dollars', y ~2500-2800). Native portrait; crops to 9:16 easily.

assets.what_it_shows: COLOUR watercolour: 4 July 1867 at American Camp, the blockhouse and US flag at left, red-coated Royal Marines and blue-coated US soldiers playing games and picnicking with women and children on the parade ground.
assets.best_segments: Optional joint-occupation beat ('they held joint picnics for 12 years'). Crop on the red and blue coats in the centre-right (x 5500-9500).
